titulo: This Hole in the Ground Breathes
tema: Why does a small hole in the South Dakota prairie breathe in and out? (Wind Cave: the cave's natural entrance blows air out or pulls it in as the outside air pressure changes)
estilo_visual: award-winning photorealistic nature photography, natural light, shallow depth of field, sharp focus, quiet empty landscape, no people

audio.como_ler: picos_cortados.trechos > 0 = distorção; silencios = buraco de 0,7 s ou mais no meio do vídeo; saltos_volume = volume muda 6 LU ou mais em 1 s; voz_abafada = trecho em que a música (ou ruído) preenche os vãos da fala (heurística: confirme pela transcrição)

cenas.narracao: A small hole in the South Dakota prairie breathes in and out.
cenas.quadro: A small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass. A thin plume of white mist flows out of the dark opening and drifts upward. The white mist plume is the brightest thing in the picture, at the center of the frame. Cold early morning light, background softly blurred.

cenas.narracao: On some days, a strong wind rushes out of it. On other days, it pulls air inside.
cenas.quadro: Low side view, close to the ground: a small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass. The grass blades beside the opening are bent away from it, all leaning in the same direction. Soft daylight, background blurred.

cenas.narracao: That hole is the natural entrance to Wind Cave, named for the wind at its mouth.
cenas.quadro: Wide view of rolling golden prairie hills under a pale blue sky. In the foreground, a low pale grey limestone outcrop with a small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass.

cenas.narracao: Early explorers heard it whistle and felt it push. Nobody could see what was pushing.
cenas.quadro: A small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass, at dusk. Deep blue twilight sky, the opening a pitch-black shadow, the grass dim and still.

cenas.narracao: But nothing down there is alive. The cave is simply answering the sky above it.
cenas.quadro: Towering dark grey storm clouds over a wide golden prairie, a low pale grey limestone outcrop in the foreground, dramatic soft light breaking through the clouds.

cenas.narracao: Behind that tiny opening lies one of the longest caves on Earth, filled with trapped air.
cenas.quadro: Inside a dark limestone cave, the low ceiling is covered in thin flat brown calcite fins that cross each other in a dense grid of small square and diamond-shaped cells. Soft warm light falls on the ceiling, and a narrow rock passage fades into darkness at the far end.

cenas.narracao: When a storm moves in, the air pressure outside drops, and the cave slowly breathes out.
cenas.quadro: Dark grey storm clouds gather low over the golden prairie. In the foreground, a small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass, with the grass blades beside it bent away from the opening.

cenas.narracao: When the weather clears and the pressure rises again, air rushes back in. The cave inhales.
cenas.quadro: Clear bright blue sky after rain. A small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass, with the grass blades now leaning in toward the opening, wet and glistening in the sunlight.

cenas.narracao: So the hole is not breathing on its own. It is the sky, breathing through the ground.
cenas.quadro: Low angle view: a small dark natural opening in pale grey limestone rock, low to the ground, surrounded by dry golden prairie grass. A thin plume of white mist rises from the opening into a wide glowing pink dawn sky. The white mist plume is the brightest thing in the picture, at the center of the frame.
cenas.movimento: mist rises slowly, very slow push-in
